title: RACK1 maintains mouse hematopoietic stem cells by directly binding to and stabilizing LDB1
task: Define RACK1 role in HSC maintenance via LDB1 stabilization
key_results: Adulthood Rack1 deletion caused rapid HSC loss with massive apoptosis; RACK1 directly binds LDB1 to prevent its ubiquitination and degradation; prenatal Rack1 deletion reduced fetal HSCs
comments: The direct RACK1–LDB1 interaction is well-characterized, but the specific contributions of this axis versus RACK1's other documented TF interactions in HSC maintenance remain partially unclear.

model_io.model: Mouse HSCs with Rack1 deletion (IFN-I-responsive cells)
Co-immunoprecipitation and ubiquitination assay

hypotheses.hypothesis: RACK1 maintains HSC fate through direct stabilization of the LDB1 adaptor
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: RACK1 binds LDB1 to suppress ubiquitination and degradation

title: Combined targeting of ER stress and CX43 preserves cardiomyocyte survival during ischemia-reperfusion
task: Establish ER stress–CX43–CHOP axis in myocardial IR injury and define protective strategy
key_results: IRE1–JNK–JDP2 pathway suppresses CX43 via AP-1 site occupancy; 4-PBA (ER stress inhibitor) combined with CX43 overexpression preserved cardiomyocyte survival in prolonged OGD/R and reduced infarct in rat IR model
comments: The dual role of CX43 (protective early, harmful late) is mechanistically interesting but suggests the therapeutic window for CX43 manipulation is narrow and context-dependent.

model_io.model: H9C2 cardiomyocytes undergoing OGD/R
Rat myocardial IR model

hypotheses.hypothesis: ER stress via IRE1–JNK–JDP2 suppresses CX43 transcription during IR injury
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: ChIP showed reciprocal JDP2/c-Jun binding at CX43 promoter AP-1 site

hypotheses.hypothesis: Combined ER stress inhibition and CX43 manipulation protects cardiomyocytes from IR injury
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 4-PBA + CX43 overexpression preserved survival in prolonged OGD/R and reduced infarction in vivo

title: ATR is a critical dependency gene for uveal melanoma
task: Identify ATR as therapeutic target in uveal melanoma
key_results: ATR inhibition (VE-822) markedly reduced colony/spheroid formation; combining ATR inhibition with paclitaxel produced significant synergy across UM models
comments: While ATR dependency is well-established in replication stress, the specific mechanistic link between S-phase completion and mitotic progression in GNAQ/GNA11-driven UM deserves deeper investigation beyond transcriptomic correlation.

model_io.model: UM cell lines (92.1, MEL270, MP38)

hypotheses.hypothesis: S-phase completion and mitotic progression determine UM cell response to ATR inhibition
hypotheses.result: Supported by RNA-seq pathway enrichment and synergy with paclitaxel

title: Sitravatinib combined with osimertinib overcomes acquired osimertinib resistance in NSCLC by targeting AXL and the PI3K/AKT/GSK3β signaling pathway
task: Overcome osimertinib resistance in EGFR-mutant NSCLC via AXL/PI3K pathway
key_results: Sitravatinib+osimertinib combination showed markedly reinforced anti-tumor activity in vitro and in vivo; suppressed AXL and PI3K/AKT/GSK3β signaling while reversing EMT
comments: The mechanism is solidly demonstrated, but the breadth of sitravatinib's multi-target activity raises questions about which kinase inhibition(s) drive the synergy and whether off-target effects contribute.

model_io.model: EGFR-mutant NSCLC cells with acquired osimertinib resistance
Nude mouse xenograft

hypotheses.hypothesis: AXL and PI3K/AKT/GSK3β pathway suppression reverses EMT-mediated osimertinib resistance
hypotheses.result: Confirmed by Western blot and functional assays

title: Multimodal radiomic and foundation-model MRI features converge on basal ganglia patterns in Parkinson’s motor subtypes
task: Discriminating Parkinson's motor subtypes (TD vs PIGD) using multimodal MRI representations
key_results: FLAIR+SWI radiomics combined with clinical scores achieved AUC=0.79±0.10; radiomic features (AUC 0.664) outperformed foundation-model embeddings (AUC 0.592)
comments: Comparative analysis of classical radiomics vs modern foundation models reveals radiomics superiority; interpretability maps pinpoint basal ganglia, supporting known PD neurobiology.

model_io.model: Radiomic feature extraction and BrainIAC transformer foundation model
inputs: T1-weighted, FLAIR, SWI, FA and MD diffusion MRI; clinical MDS-UPDRS scores
outputs: 1046 radiomic features and 2048-dim embeddings per modality

model_io.model: Machine learning classifiers (nested 5-fold CV with PCA dimension reduction)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multimodal MRI can discriminate objective biological differences between motor subtypes
hypotheses.result: Best model (FLAIR+SWI radiomics+clinical) achieved AUC 0.79; SWI intensity/texture and basal ganglia regions drive discrimination

hypotheses.hypothesis: Foundation-model embeddings outperform conventional radiomics
hypotheses.result: Radiomics significantly outperformed embeddings (0.664 vs 0.592 AUC)

title: A hybrid deep feature optimized ensemble framework for multiclass skin disease classification

key_results: ResBR-XGBR framework achieved 95.2%±0.5% test accuracy; ResNet50+Boruta/RFE features with ensemble classifiers outperformed standalone learners

Ensemble (Random Forest + XGBoost)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Random serum LH is the dominant predictor

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multi-epitope design targeting conserved, antigenic Mtb proteins induces robust immunity
hypotheses.result: Generated 429-aa construct with stable 3D fold and strong TLR signaling (TLR4 binding –1175.2 kcal/mol)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Vaccine construct preferentially activates TLR4 over TLR2
hypotheses.result: TLR4 affinity (–1175.2 kcal/mol) substantially higher than TLR2 (–1022.8 kcal/mol); MD confirmed stable interactions with both

task: Discovery of allosteric PCSK9 inhibitors via graph neural networks and structure-based modeling

title: An exploratory survey of barriers and enablers of AI adoption in rural and urban dental practices in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Germany
task: Barriers and enablers of AI adoption in rural and urban dental practices in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Germany
key_results: Among 163 dental practitioners (55% rural), majority use digital records and appointment systems; minority implemented AI; perceived barriers include additional costs, increased workload concerns, and limited familiarity
comments: Exploratory baseline assessment captures underrepresented low-digitalization practices; findings are regionally specific and generalizability to other healthcare sectors or regions is unclear.

model_io.model: Questionnaire-based survey with descriptive analysis
inputs: dental practice owner responses on digital infrastructure, AI use, perceived adoption barriers

hypotheses.hypothesis: Perceived additional costs, workload concerns, and limited AI familiarity are primary adoption barriers

hypotheses.hypothesis: Four-switch inverter topology reduces switching losses and component complexity versus six-switch topology
